Context: https://github.com/swc-project/swc/pull/2776#discussion_r751427342

With effort for the #2716, there seems some overlapping between few visitors to handle replacing context specific (`this`, etcs). It maybe possible we could reuse instead of repeating same steps.

Probably reusing `ThisReplacer`, and moreover potentially make a single visitor instead fo `This` + `Arguments`. But it requires proper audit to do so.

review_comments: This has exponential time complexity, but it's fine for most case because `n` is super small. I think it's better to have a comment mentioning it.
This can be removed, as `f.visit_mut_children_with(self);` is default behavior.
I think you can implement `visit_mut_prop_name` which only visits children if it's `PropName::Computed`.
No I can't, since I want args and function body in getter/setter/method be ignored
Could you explain why this is exponential?

Because `FunctionWrapper` visits an expression deeply.

For 

```js
const arrow = (a = (b = (c = () => this) => {})) => ({}) => {};
```

the innermost `this` expression will be visited by `FunctionWrapper` once per `visit_mut_expr` of an arrow expression.

e.g. Twice due to `c = (() => this) => {}`. 

 - once by `params.visit_mut_with(self);`
 - once by `params.visit_mut_with(&mut FunctionWrapper::new(&mut self.state));`)

I was confused, so I made a benchmark that only profiles nested visitor.
You can see the content of benchmark at https://github.com/swc-project/swc/pull/2820/files and



This is what I get.


Note: In this benchmark, the operation of nested visitor is very simple
I see, maybe I could figure out a way to avoid this
Wait, wouldn't swc translate the innermost arrow expression first, and every time a `FunctionWrapper` is started, it will be stopped to visit inner arrow by `FnExpr`?
See the new test in the new commit, only 6 expressions is printed, I guess it's fine

The time expression printed does not matter.
At the benchmark above I posted, `visit count` is also tested.
It's exponential because it's deeply nested, not because a node is visited exponential times.
